key_insight: A frozen, general-purpose LLM can propose promising quantum-circuit parameters when Hamiltonians have identifiable structure, but performs worse than Adam on general random Hamiltonians.
engineering_relevance: LLM-generated circuit parameters enable independently verifiable energy calculations, making them more trustworthy engineering outputs than direct energy predictions.
method: Generate complete circuit parameter vectors from symbolic circuit and Hamiltonian descriptions.
Optionally provide iterative energy feedback and compare performance with Adam optimization.
Evaluate random Hamiltonians, structured parent Hamiltonians, molecular systems, and blind circuit interpretation.
evidence_signal: Evaluations found larger energy errors than Adam for general Hamiltonians, limited gains from feedback, and promising low-energy configurations for structured Hamiltonians.
watch_item: Direct LLM energy predictions can violate spectral lower bounds, so independently evaluate generated circuit parameters rather than trusting predicted energies.
paper_title: Programming Quantum Circuit Parameters with Large Language Models
